purpose: Does the shipped 3.0.0 lean debugger text (release candidate commit 293491f8) keep the 2.0.1 text's F-code agreement, root-cause match, attribution and unsupported-claim rate on a new, larger corpus of 107 labeled failures (75 restated from real merged fixes, 32 authored to cover the F-codes real fixes rarely show), after the v7 check on 28 cases failed only because its F-code interval was too wide? This measures interpretation of the skill text only: safety, redaction, launcher, acquisition and any tool use are not exercised, so no safety or workflow claim can come from it.
naming: v8 follows v7 (same arms, judges, margins and guards) and replaces its corpus, its new-text snapshot and its F-code evaluation set. v7 is kept as run; its FAIL is not rewritten.

arms.new-lean: skill-snapshots/new: the same commit, SKILL.md + references/artifact-extraction.md + classification-procedure.md + fix-verification.md. The typical diagnosis path of the 3.0.0 loading rules. Primary arm.
arms.old: skill-snapshots/old: git tag v2.0.1 (20cc5fc8), SKILL.md + every file in references/ (seven files per framework). The released text; byte-identical to the v7 old snapshot.
arms.free: taxonomy-free prompt (v2 FREE_FRAME), 3-field schema, no skill text. Reported only, never a gate.

corpus: benchmarks/debugger-skill-effect-v8/corpus.json: 107 labeled failures (73 Playwright, 34 Cypress). 75 are restated from public merged fixes in 67 repositories (MIT/Apache/BSD, merged 2026-07-27 to 2026-10-16; none appears in the v1 to v7 corpora or in the OpenMetadata reports that tuned 2.0.1), each from the maintainers' own PR text and diff; 28 were prepared first and 47 were added in an extension after the first 60 gave too small a primary set (extension/). 32 are authored artifacts built from the F-code definitions to cover codes that real fixes rarely show (F1, F4, F6, F9, F10, F13 and a few more); they are labeled by construction before any model call and are reported separately.
corpus_history: New in v8: no case was used in v1 to v7. The F-code labels were set by one author from the maintainers' fix (real) or the construction design (authored), using only the F1-F15 definitions that old and new share; the classification-procedure.md files, which differ between old and new, were not used. Blind second mapper (done 2026-10-16, before any scoring call; five calls, one per batch): codex gpt-6-sol (cli 0.159.3), zero-tool, 2026-10-16; it saw only the root-cause statement and the fix and agreed with the author label on 54 of the first 60 cases and, in four further zero-tool calls on the extension cases, on 28 of 47; the 25 disagreements are listed in labels-final.json and leave the primary F-code set, not the corpus. The F-code check runs on the cases where the mapper agreed with the author (labels-final.json, status final). The author is not independent of the benchmark: the 32 authored cases follow the taxonomy's canonical patterns, so they are probably easier than real failures; they are reported as a separate stratum. The extension was added after the first 60 and before any scoring call because the first preparation gave 54 primary cases; the extension cases were selected by size and file filters fixed before labeling, labeled from the merged fix, and mapped by the same blind procedure; the author knew the primary set was below 80 while adding the last batches. 6 of the 8 extension cases the author labeled F12 were read as F2 by the mapper (the author/mapper boundary differs there); they leave the primary set and were not relabeled.

host.cli_version_policy: minimum (a floor, never an exact build; AGENTS.md: exact pins strand a protocol)

judge.blind: sees maintainers' explanation and fix (match) or the excerpt (ground) plus all nine candidate root-cause statements per case under letter ids in shuffled order; never sees arm, model, repetition or F-code
judge.match: v2 2/1/0 mechanism rubric on root_cause only
judge.ground: count of claims in root_cause not supported by the excerpt

judge_retry.rule: A judge answer that does not parse or omits any candidate id is asked again with the identical frame and candidate order, up to three attempts in total. This is registered before any call because the v6 run lost 14 of 390 calls to one omitting answer and needed a post hoc re-judge. A still-incomplete entry leaves its candidates unjudged and the verdict INCONCLUSIVE.

decision_rule.PASS: all calls scored and judged, no digest or prompt-digest mismatch, and every check holds for new-lean minus old: (1) strict-match paired difference 95% case-cluster bootstrap lower bound >= -0.05; (2) its point estimate >= -0.05; (3) F-code exact paired difference on the primary label set (cases where the blind second mapper agreed with the author label), 95% lower bound >= -0.10; (4) product/test diagnosis accuracy >= old - 0.05; (5) unsupported claims per answer new-lean - old <= +0.30; (6) new-lean total input tokens <= 0.80 x old.
decision_rule.FAIL: all calls scored and judged and any check false
decision_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: any unscored model call after the retry policy, any unparsed or incomplete judge entry after the judge retry policy, any input or prompt digest mismatch, or a canary report
decision_rule.secondary: new-full minus old and new-lean minus new-full were dropped before the freeze (see revision_drop_new_full); H2 and H3 are not run. F-code differences are also reported, descriptively, on four other sets: all labeled cases, real cases only, authored cases only, and the cases the author marked as a clean fit. free is compared descriptively with the same paired statistics.
decision_rule.wording: A PASS supports exactly one sentence: on these 107 development cases the shipped 3.0.0 lean text was not worse than the 2.0.1 text on zero-tool diagnosis by more than the stated margins, at about the stated share of the input tokens. A FAIL on check 3 with a lower bound below -0.10 is recorded as FAIL and read as 'not proven', not as a measured loss; it is not rescued by a different set or margin. It never supports 'better', 'safer', or any statement about the full workflow.

power: Declared before data; see power-simulation.json and power-simulation.py. v7 measured the F-code paired difference at -0.029 (95% interval -0.116 to +0.058) on 23 labeled cases, with 16 of 23 tied. Resampling those 23 differences, a primary set of 82 cases (the blind-mapper agreement set) passes the -0.10 lower-bound check in about 97 of 100 trials if the true difference is 0, 89 if it is -0.02, 67 if it is -0.04 and 41 if it is -0.06; 80 percent power needs about 40 cases at 0, 63 at -0.02 and 77 at the v7 point estimate. The first 60 cases alone (54 primary) would have passed in 89, 75 and 54 of 100 trials at 0, -0.02 and -0.04. This corpus is powered to confirm a small or zero loss, not to prove a loss of 0.04 to 0.06 is absent; a second run with more cases is the planned follow-up if the interval straddles -0.10.
validity: Every prompt's prompt_sha256 must equal the digest recomputed from the frozen snapshot, frame and excerpt (analyze refuses otherwise): this is the proof that each arm saw its declared skill text.

Calls, infrastructure errors, retries, schema violations (prediction_error) and unjudged candidates are counted and printed; the verdict requires zero infrastructure errors, zero invalid predictions and zero unjudged candidates, and reports the retry counts.
The judges are blind to arm by construction (candidate letters only); tests assert that no judge prompt contains an arm name.
A freeze marker (freeze.json) binds protocol.json and this script; run, canary, judge and analyze refuse if either changed.
The CLI is checked against a minimum version before any model call; no exact build is pinned.
A canary (2 cases x 4 arms x 1 repetition = 8 calls, non-data) must return PROCEED from validate-canary before run.
No campaign lock, browser, Docker or port is used, so this harness can run beside the thin-eval driver (whose process probe only matches run-generator-*.py).
labels-final.json must have status 'final' (a blind second mapper's output applied by apply-blind-labels.py) before freeze; freeze refuses a provisional file, and the file is digest-bound.
The shipped-text snapshot is a committed tree (293491f8), not a working directory; the old snapshot is byte-identical to the v7 old snapshot, which was built from tag v2.0.1.
tuning_audit: Question: was the 3.0.0 debugger text tuned on these cases? Method: (1) grep skills/playwright-debugger and skills/cypress-debugger at 293491f8 for the 107 case ids and the 67 full source repository names (174 patterns, rerun after the extension): zero hits (the short names 'cypress' and 'console' match ordinary words and are not hits); (2) order of events: the debugger text was last changed by commit d357338f (2026-10-16) and the real fixes were collected after it, on 2026-10-16, from PRs merged 2026-07-27 to 2026-10-16; the text was not edited afterwards. What this cannot rule out: the real fixes existed (merged July to October) before the text was written, and the author of the corpus had read the F1-F15 table before writing the authored cases. Rule for the run: any edit to skills/*-debugger after the snapshot invalidates this protocol and requires a new version.
limits: Zero-tool prompts measure interpretation of the text, not the report reader, the downloader, the launcher, redaction or any safety gate; new-lean deliberately omits safety-procedures.md, so this benchmark cannot show that the conditional load works.

32 of 107 cases are authored by the benchmark's author from the taxonomy's canonical patterns; they are expected to be easier than real failures and share the author's reading of the F-code definitions. They are reported as a separate stratum and are not claimed as real-world evidence.

F-code truth is one author's label plus a blind second model mapper; there is no human adjudication. Some codes overlap in the taxonomy itself (F1/F14, F2/F12, F3/F10): 'forced' cases are marked in label-ledger.json and the agreement set removes the ones the mapper reads differently.
Truth for real cases is the merged fix; several PR descriptions were written with AI assistants. Both judges are models. One host (Claude sonnet), one judge family, three repetitions.
old loads SKILL.md plus six references while new-lean loads SKILL.md plus three: the arms differ in how much text they see by design, not only in wording.
The corpus is a development set. It is not hidden or sealed and must not be described as a holdout.
claim_limits: zero-tool diagnosis from a sanitized excerpt; no tool use, no safety behavior
107 cases (75 real, 32 authored), one host, three repetitions; not a holdout
non-inferiority within the stated margins; no superiority claim

canary.verdict: validate-canary returns PROCEED only if all six calls exist (two per arm), none has an infrastructure error, a retry, a missing usage record or an invalid prediction, and every prompt digest matches the frozen material; the report is marked canary and analyze/judge refuse it

run_order: (blind step, owner/agent) give blind-labels/INSTRUCTIONS.md to a second model mapper; save its JSON; python3 benchmarks/debugger-skill-effect-v8/apply-blind-labels.py MAPPER.json --mapper '<runner/model>'

revision_drop_new_full.decided_by: owner, in chat, before the freeze and before any v8 model call
revision_drop_new_full.what: The descriptive arm new-full (3.0.0 SKILL.md plus every reference, the worst-case text load) is removed from the schedule, the canary, the analysis and the comparisons. The primary comparison (new-lean minus old, five checks including the token check) and the descriptive comparisons with free are unchanged.
revision_drop_new_full.why: new-full is descriptive and never part of the verdict; dropping it cuts the model run from 1284 to 963 calls and saves about a quarter of the Claude usage, which was already high.
consequences: H2 (new-full not worse than old) and H3 (new-lean not worse than new-full) are not run and are not reported; the worst-case load stays described by bytes only (57,260 / 56,230 bytes, the arm_bytes_dropped_arm entry).
The skill-snapshots/new files stay as they are because new-lean reads them; the new-full arm_material digests are removed from frozen_digests.
The canary becomes 6 calls (2 cases x 3 arms x 1 repetition).
revision_drop_new_full.dropped_arm_description: skill-snapshots/new: git commit 293491f8 of branch release/3.0.0-candidate (the shipped candidate), SKILL.md + every file in references/ (seven files per framework). Worst-case load; descriptive.
not_changed: corpus, labels, power simulation, margins, guards, judges, seed
